title: Helix: Serving Large Language Models over Heterogeneous GPUs and Network via Max-Flow
technique: Max-flow formulation of LLM serving over heterogeneous GPUs/network; MILP for model placement plus per-request flow-based pipeline scheduling (IWRR)

optimized_metrics.evidence: Helix then uses a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) algorithm to discover highly optimized strategies ... maximizes the max flow, thus maximizing serving throughput.

headline_claim.text: Helix improves serving throughput by up to 3.3× and reduces prompting and decoding latency by up to 66% and 24%, respectively, compared to existing approaches.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 6-10 average decode throughput (offline and online)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For offline serving, we report average decode throughput, which is the number of tokens generated per second.
metric_definitions.notes: output tokens only; whole-cluster throughput, not per GPU

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For online serving, we further report average prompt latency and decode latency, which is the average latency for parsing user input and generating new tokens, respectively.
metric_definitions.notes: prompt latency ~ TTFT-like and decode latency ~ per-token latency but definition is brief; whether queueing is included not stated

load_regime: online: Azure Conversation arrival times scaled to 75% of cluster peak throughput; offline: requests arrive at rate that fully utilizes the cluster
tradeoff_acknowledged: Helix trades some latency for throughput in places: e.g. decode latency 10-16% higher than Swarm in some single-cluster/geo cases because of higher GPU utilization; SP baseline has lower average latency in some settings because it serves mostly on fast GPUs
hardware: heterogeneous clusters of 24-42 nodes (A100, L4, T4 and others, up to 7 node types), real cluster plus simulator (avg decode-throughput error <5%)
workloads: Azure Conversation arrivals, offline dataset inference
extractor_notes: Optimization target is max serving throughput (max-flow value); latency is claimed in the abstract and evaluated but is not in the MILP objective, so latency entries are weak/derived (see locators). Both latencies are averages; no tail percentiles.
load_class_quote: 'We refer to the two settings as online and offline serving.' (§6.1): offline = requests at the rate needed to fully utilize the cluster; online = Azure Conversation arrivals at 75% of peak
repass_log: THR_TOK second entry (result headline 'improves serving throughput by up to 3.3x') dropped as duplicate of MILP/max-flow design entry

TTFT (prompt latency) and TPOT (decode latency) demoted to reported: only abstract 'low-latency' claim; latency not in MILP objective and paper asks 'Does Helix sacrifice latency for throughput?' (Sec. 6.3); reported as averages ('average prompt latency and decode latency')
